project.name: c-blosc2
project.fixed_commit_note: The staged patch is source-grounded to the reproduced path: it moves `ctx->literalsPtr++` before the extended literal-length decode and adds explicit `iend - 2` / `iend - 3` bounds checks before the 16-bit and 24-bit extension reads in `internal-complibs/lizard-1.0/lizard_decompress_liz.h`. Stage 01 did not save a fixed-build rerun, so this role treats the patch as corroborating source evidence rather than dynamically confirmed remediation.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42489779 (c-blosc2): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 2 found by fuzz target decompress_chunk_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42489779
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue description / reproduction_report.json / staged patch.diff / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged 78-byte witness first reaches project code in `blosc_cbuffer_sizes()`, which decodes `nbytes = 32`, `blocksize = 32`, and `cbytes = 78` from header bytes 4-15. The harness and `blosc_cbuffer_validate()` admit the chunk because those outer-header values are internally consistent. During decompression, `initialize_context_decompression()` re-reads flag byte `0xbd`, so `blosc_d()` treats the chunk as an extended-header single-block `BLOSC_LIZARD_FORMAT` payload with `bstarts[0] = 36`, yielding one 38-byte compressed block that begins at input byte 40. Inside `Lizard_decompress_generic()`, block byte 41 is `res = 0x20`, so `Lizard_readStream()` treats both the flags and literals streams as raw 24-bit-length streams; bytes 67-69 describe a 4-byte flags stream `ff 20 20 20`, and bytes 74-76 describe a 1-byte literals stream containing only `0xff`, making `ctx->literalsPtr == iend - 1` before `Lizard_decompress_LIZv1()` starts. The first token byte `0xff` requests extended literal-length decoding. The line-63 guard checks only `ctx->literalsPtr > iend - 1`, so it accepts the last-byte sentinel and falls through without proving that the three extension bytes required by the `0xff` case exist. Line 64 then reads the sentinel `0xff`, line 65 takes the `length >= 254` branch, line 69 takes the `length != 254` branch, and line 70 calls `MEM_readLE24(ctx->literalsPtr+1)`. `MEM_readLE24()` immediately performs `MEM_readLE16()` from one byte past the 78-byte input, matching the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2 in `Lizard_decompress_LIZv1`. The fix commit `3724317f7bd698abb3b3d39a6d785088b9f8db0a` hardens this exact path by incrementing `ctx->literalsPtr` earlier and by adding explicit bounds checks for both the 16-bit (`0xfe`) and 24-bit (`0xff`) extension encodings.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled Blosc header sizes that the harness and `blosc_cbuffer_validate()` use to admit the chunk into decompression.
source.value_from: The exact staged 78-byte blob in `gt_results/arvo_42489779/poc` (SHA-256 `9f697661c81196af000d2a19a57133002761a29f554ed4b289ffb2d5d50885e2`) first reaches project code through `blosc_cbuffer_sizes()`. Header bytes 4-7 `20 00 00 00` decode to `nbytes = 32`, bytes 8-11 `20 00 00 00` decode to `blocksize = 32`, and bytes 12-15 `4e 00 00 00` decode to `cbytes = 78`. Those values satisfy the harness gate `cbytes == size && nbytes != 0`, then `blosc_cbuffer_validate()` rechecks them before `blosc2_decompress()` later re-parses header byte 2 `0xbd` and block-start entry `36`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Exact source-level read of the attacker-controlled sentinel that drives the overflowing extension decode. On the witnessed block, the one-byte literals stream contains only `0xff`, so this statement materializes `length = 255` while `ctx->literalsPtr` is still the final byte of the input.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The preceding literals-stream descriptor bytes `01 00 00` make `ctx->literalsPtr` point to the single final input byte 77, whose value in the staged witness is `0xff`.

root_cause.description: This is the only bounds guard executed before the extended literal-length decoder reads the sentinel and chooses between the 16-bit and 24-bit extension formats. The false branch proves only that the sentinel byte itself exists; it does not prove that `ctx->literalsPtr + 1` has the extra bytes required by the `0xfe` or `0xff` encodings.
root_cause.note: The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by moving `ctx->literalsPtr++` ahead of the extension decode and adding explicit `ctx->literalsPtr > iend - 2` / `ctx->literalsPtr > iend - 3` checks for the `0xfe` and `0xff` cases.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The `0xff` extension case reads a 24-bit literal length starting one byte past the end of the one-byte literals stream.
sink.note: On the witnessed path, line 63 falls through with `ctx->literalsPtr == iend - 1`, line 64 reads sentinel `0xff`, and the `length != 254` branch selects this 24-bit extension read while `ctx->literalsPtr` still points at byte 77. `MEM_readLE24()` begins with `MEM_readLE16(memPtr)`, so the first operation is a 2-byte read from bytes 78-79, matching the saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` in `Lizard_decompress_LIZv1`.

parser_admitted.description: After the outer Blosc header and block table are accepted, the only block is dispatched into the vulnerable inner parser: `compformat` resolves to `BLOSC_LIZARD_FORMAT`, `cbytes = 38`, and `src` already points at the block payload beginning at testcase byte 40.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzzer buffer first enters project code through `blosc_cbuffer_sizes()`, which reads `nbytes = 32`, `blocksize = 32`, and `cbytes = 78` from the outer header; `blosc_cbuffer_validate()` rechecks those values and admits the 78-byte chunk.
The decompressor re-reads flag byte `0xbd`, re-materializes the same header sizes, computes `nblocks = 1`, and uses the extended-header layout to locate `bstarts[0] = 36`.
Block 0 uses `src_offset = 36`, reads block `cbytes = 38`, advances to testcase byte 40, and dispatches the block to the Lizard backend because `compformat == BLOSC_LIZARD_FORMAT`.

The Lizard block control byte `res = 0x20` makes the flags and literals streams raw 24-bit-length streams; the flags stream becomes `ff 20 20 20`, and the literals stream is the single final byte `ff`.

The first token `0xff` enters extended literal-length decoding. The line-63 guard only checks `ctx->literalsPtr > iend - 1`, so it falls through on the last-byte sentinel without proving that any extension bytes exist.

`length = *ctx->literalsPtr` reads `0xff`, the `length >= 254` and `length != 254` branches select the 24-bit extension case, and `MEM_readLE24(ctx->literalsPtr + 1)` performs the out-of-bounds read recorded by AddressSanitizer.

fine_trace.note: Source. `blosc_cbuffer_sizes()` first materializes the attacker-controlled outer-header sizes: `nbytes = 32`, `blocksize = 32`, and `cbytes = 78`. The harness continues only because these values satisfy `cbytes == size && nbytes != 0`.

Outer-header admission. `blosc_cbuffer_validate()` re-reads the same header and returns success because `header_cbytes = 78` matches the supplied `cbytes` and `*nbytes = 32` is below `BLOSC_MAX_BUFFERSIZE`; the harness therefore calls `blosc2_decompress()` on the same blob.

After admission, the decompressor re-reads header flag byte `0xbd` into `context->header_flags`. Its top three bits decode to `BLOSC_LIZARD_FORMAT`, and the low bits set both shuffle flags, selecting the extended-header block-table layout.

The same header bytes are copied into the decompression context: `context->sourcesize = 32`, `context->blocksize = 32`, and local `cbytes = 78`. Those values seed the later block-count and bounds arithmetic.
From the re-parsed sizes, the chunk contains exactly one block: `nblocks = 1` and `leftover = 0`.
Because both shuffle bits are set, the extended-header branch places the block-start table at byte 32. `context->bstarts` therefore points at the witness entry `24 00 00 00`, so `bstarts[0] = 36`.

fine_trace.code: int32_t src_offset = memcpyed ? BLOSC_MAX_OVERHEAD + j * context->blocksize : sw32_(bstarts + j);
fine_trace.note: For the only block `j = 0`, `serial_blosc()` reads `src_offset = 36`, so the compressed block header begins at testcase byte 36.
At block offset 36, the 4-byte per-block header decodes to `cbytes = 38`. After `src += sizeof(int32_t)`, `src` advances to testcase byte 40, the start of the 38-byte Lizard payload.
The backend selector is derived from `context->header_flags`. For header byte `0xbd`, the top three bits yield `compformat = 5`, i.e. `BLOSC_LIZARD_FORMAT`.
Parser admission into the vulnerable inner codec. Because `compformat == BLOSC_LIZARD_FORMAT`, `blosc_d()` passes the 38-byte block from step 8 into `lizard_wrap_decompress()` with `neblock = 32`.

The first Lizard block control byte is `0x20`. It is not `LIZARD_FLAG_UNCOMPRESSED`, has no `LIZARD_FLAG_LEN` bit set, and clears both `LIZARD_FLAG_FLAGS` and `LIZARD_FLAG_LITERALS`, so the next flags and literals streams are interpreted as raw 24-bit-length streams.

fine_trace.code:
streamLen = Lizard_readStream(res&LIZARD_FLAG_FLAGS, &ip, iend, decompFlagsBase, decompFlagsBase + LIZARD_HUF_BLOCK_SIZE, &ctx.flagsPtr, &ctx.flagsEnd, LIZARD_STREAM_FLAGS);
if (streamLen == 0) goto _output_error;
fine_trace.note: With `(res & LIZARD_FLAG_FLAGS) == 0`, `Lizard_readStream()` treats bytes 67-69 `04 00 00` as the raw flags-stream length. `ctx.flagsPtr` therefore spans bytes 70-73 `ff 20 20 20`.

fine_trace.code:
streamLen = Lizard_readStream(res&LIZARD_FLAG_LITERALS, &ip, iend, decompLiteralsBase, decompLiteralsBase + LIZARD_HUF_BLOCK_SIZE, &ctx.literalsPtr, &ctx.literalsEnd, LIZARD_STREAM_LITERALS);
if (streamLen == 0) goto _output_error;
fine_trace.note: With `(res & LIZARD_FLAG_LITERALS) == 0`, `Lizard_readStream()` treats bytes 74-76 `01 00 00` as the raw literals-stream length. The only literal byte is byte 77 `0xff`, so `ctx->literalsPtr == iend - 1` and `ctx->literalsEnd == iend`.
The first sequence token read from the flags stream is `0xff`. Since `token >= 32` and `(token & MAX_SHORT_LITLEN) == 7`, `Lizard_decompress_LIZv1()` enters the extended literal-length decode path.

Root cause. This guard executes before line 64 reads the sentinel byte. With `ctx->literalsPtr == iend - 1`, the condition is false and control falls through on the last-byte sentinel, but the code still has not proved that the extra bytes at `ctx->literalsPtr + 1` required by the `0xfe` or `0xff` extensions exist. The fix moves `ctx->literalsPtr++` earlier and adds explicit `iend - 2` / `iend - 3` checks inside those branches.
Tainted value origin. The only literal-stream byte is also `0xff`, so `length` becomes 255 while `ctx->literalsPtr` still points at the final byte of the input.
Because `length = 255`, the decoder enters the extended-length subpath that will read extra bytes from `ctx->literalsPtr + 1`.
The sentinel is `0xff`, not `0xfe`, so the `length == 254` arm is skipped and the `else` arm selects the 24-bit extension read at line 70.

Sink. The false branch from line 63 (`ctx->literalsPtr <= iend - 1`) and the `length != 254` branch reach `MEM_readLE24(ctx->literalsPtr+1)` while `ctx->literalsPtr` still points at byte 77. `MEM_readLE24()` begins by calling `MEM_readLE16(memPtr)`, so the first operation is a 2-byte out-of-bounds read from bytes 78-79, matching the saved AddressSanitizer crash.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch directly adds the missing bounds checks for the `0xfe` and `0xff` literal-length extensions and moves `ctx->literalsPtr++` earlier in this block. Stage 02 did not run the fixed build, so `patch_resolves` remains false here.

evidence_limitations: Stage 01 reproduced only the vulnerable build. There is no saved fixed-build rerun for this sample, so `patch_resolves` remains false despite the patch being source-grounded to the reproduced path.

The saved ASan trace names `Lizard_decompress_LIZv1` and the header file but does not print an exact source line inside the inlined header. Sink line 70 is source-grounded from the witness bytes, the vulnerable control flow, and the recorded 2-byte read size.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved `reproduction_report.json` records `docker exec gt-arvo_42489779-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'` returning 1 with `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` in `Lizard_decompress_LIZv1`, matching OSS-Fuzz issue 42489779.

format.name: 78-byte Blosc chunk with a one-byte Lizard literals stream
format.contract: Exactly the staged 78-byte blob stored in `poc` (SHA-256 `9f697661c81196af000d2a19a57133002761a29f554ed4b289ffb2d5d50885e2`). Relevant bytes are: Blosc header byte 2 `0xbd` (`BLOSC_LIZARD_FORMAT` with the extended-header layout), header bytes 4-7 `20 00 00 00` (`nbytes = 32`), bytes 8-11 `20 00 00 00` (`blocksize = 32`), bytes 12-15 `4e 00 00 00` (`cbytes = 78`), bytes 32-35 `24 00 00 00` (`bstarts[0] = 36`), and bytes 36-39 `26 00 00 00` (block `cbytes = 38`). Within that 38-byte Lizard block, byte 40 is compression level `0x2f`, byte 41 is `res = 0x20`, bytes 67-69 encode a 4-byte flags stream whose first flag byte is `0xff`, and bytes 74-76 encode a 1-byte literals stream whose only byte is `0xff`. Those exact values make `ctx->literalsPtr == iend - 1`, make the first token request extended literal-length decoding, and make the decoder take the unchecked `MEM_readLE24(ctx->literalsPtr+1)` path. Stage 01 only proves this exact blob and observed path; this contract does not generalize to nearby Blosc headers, other Lizard stream layouts, or alternate literal-length sentinels.
